verdict.rationale: GitHub documents its own automation and background-agent capabilities. GitHub Actions automates repository workflows, and Copilot cloud agent takes assigned tasks and runs them in GitHub-hosted cloud sandboxes "without using your machine", returning pull requests (issue → agent → PR). The evidence shows one-off delegated tasks and generic workflow automation, but it never documents recurring schedules or event triggers for these automations, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documented recurring/scheduled or event-triggered autonomous runs, explicit detail on how background automations are configured, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Automate, customize, and execute your software development workflows right in your repository with GitHub Actions.
Cloud sandboxes are isolated environments that GitHub hosts, where Copilot runs your cloud sessions without using your machine.
A change can start as an issue, be picked up by an agent, return as a pull request, get reviewed for quality and security, and be merged.
Copilot can research a repository, create an implementation plan, and make code changes on a branch.
